key_insight: The paper shows that nonsmooth, nonconvex stochastic optimization with convex constraints can still achieve optimal convergence rates to a ,ε-Goldstein stationary point, matching the best known unconstrained behavior.
engineering_relevance: This gives a theoretically optimal foundation for constrained large-scale optimization routines in machine learning and scientific computing, including settings where gradients are noisy, nonsmooth, or only available through zeroth-order queries.
method: Projection-based and projection-free stochastic algorithms for constrained optimization.
Reduction of the constrained nonconvex problem to online linear optimization.
Lower-bound analysis via the Frank-Wolfe gap, including smooth cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports optimal O(δ^{-1}ε^{-3}) stochastic-gradient complexity and O(dδ^{-1}ε^{-3}) zeroth-order complexity, with matching lower bounds.
watch_item: The guarantees are asymptotic and rely on convex constraint sets plus access assumptions (stochastic gradients or zeroth-order queries), so practical performance may depend on projection/Frank-Wolfe implementation costs and sampling noise.
paper_title: Optimal Algorithms for Nonsmooth Nonconvex Stochastic Optimization with Constraints
